## Findings
- claim-1: The original linear system has variables \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\lambda\subseteq b^a\), \(|\lambda|<N\), and \(\theta\subseteq(n-r)^r\), \(|\theta|=N-|\lambda|\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 285-303]
- claim-2: The published large-\(N\) step enlarges \(\varphi\), then asserts that setting selected enlarged variables to zero recovers the original equations. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-818]
- claim-3: The proposed projected-wide-row repair that discards \(\theta\nsubseteq(q-i)^j\) is false: it discards an original variable \(A_{\varnothing,(2)}\). Take \[ (n,r,i,j,a,b,N)=(6,3,2,2,1,2,2),\qquad q=n-r=3. \] This is valid since \[ a+j=3=r,\quad a+i=3=q,\quad b=2\le i,j,\quad N=2=ab. \] The original variables are exactly \[ x=A_{\varnothing,(2)},\qquad y=A_{\varnothing,(1,1)},\qquad z=A_{(1),(1)}. \] Since \((q-i)^j=(1,1)\), the original variable \(x\) is excluded by the proposed projection. The original decomposable partitions of weight \(ij+N=6\) are \[ (3,3),\quad(3,2,1)\quad\text{(wide)},\qquad(2,2,2)\quad\text{(tall)}. \] Pieri gives their rows, in column order \((x,y,z)\), \[ \operatorname{Lin}(3,3)=(0,1,0),\quad \operatorname{Lin}(3,2,1)=(1,1,1),\quad \operatorname{Lin}(2,2,2)=(1,0,1). \] Hence the original wide-row lattice is \[ W=\mathbb Z(0,1,0)+\mathbb Z(1,1,1). \] For the first enlargement \[ (\widehat n,\widehat r,\widehat j)=(24,6,4), \] the partition \[ \tau=(4,2,2,2) \] is enlarged-wide and decomposable. Retaining **all** original variables in its row gives \[ P_{\rm all}\bigl(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau)\bigr) =(1,0,0), \] because \[ c_{(2^4),(2)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=1,\qquad c_{(2^4),(1,1)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=0,\qquad c_{(2^4,1),(1)}^{(4,2,2,2)}=0. \] But \((1,0,0)\notin W\): if \[ (1,0,0)=u(0,1,0)+v(1,1,1), \] then the first coordinate gives \(v=1\), whereas the third gives \(v=0\), a contradiction.
- claim-4: Therefore the asserted alternative “every enlarged wide row projects to an original wide row or zero” fails once every original variable is retained. In particular, the required extension-of-solutions argument is not supplied by the cited enlargement procedure.
- claim-5: No alternative all-valid-parameter proof of the original large-\(N\) inconsistency is provided here.
## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\) and retain the full original variable lattice
\[
X_\varphi=\bigoplus_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a,\ |\lambda|<N\\
\theta\subseteq q^r,\ |\theta|=N-|\lambda|}}
\mathbb Z A_{\lambda,\theta}.
\]
No condition \(\theta\subseteq(q-i)^j\) is imposed. Thus for
\((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)=(6,3,2,2,1,2,2)\),
\[
(A_{\varnothing,(2)},A_{\varnothing,(1,1)},A_{(1),(1)})
\]
are all retained.

Let \(\overline\Lambda=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) and
\[
T(A_{\lambda,\theta})=\bar s_\lambda\otimes\bar s_\theta.
\]
Schur bases make \(T|_{X_\varphi}\) injective. For a decomposable row with components \((B,R)\), the source proves
\[
T(\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu))
=\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_B\otimes\bar s_R)
\]
[doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 428-493].

For a tall \(\rho\), let \(\beta=\rho_B\). Then
\(\beta\subseteq b^a\), \(|\beta|=N\), and
\[
T(\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\rho))
=\mathrm{CP}(\bar s_\beta\otimes1).
\]
The integral Hopf identity
\[
\mathrm{CP}(s_\beta\otimes1)=
\sum_{\substack{\lambda,\mu\\\mu\ne\varnothing}}
(-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\,
\mathrm{CP}(s_\lambda\otimes s_{\mu'})
\tag{*}
\]
holds in \(\Lambda\otimes\Lambda\). Indeed, coassociativity and
\(S(s_\mu)=(-1)^{|\mu|}s_{\mu'}\) give
\[
\sum_{\lambda,\mu}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}
\Delta(s_\lambda)(1\otimes S(s_\mu))=s_\beta\otimes1.
\]
The \(\mu=\varnothing\) summand is \(\Delta(s_\beta)\); rearrangement gives \((*)\). The antipode formula is supplied at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 702-735].

For each nonzero term of \((*)\), \(c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\ne0\) implies
\[
\lambda,\mu\subseteq\beta,\qquad |\lambda|<N.
\]
Set \(R=\mu'\), pad \(R\) to \(j\) rows and \(\lambda\) to \(a\) rows, and define
\[
\nu_{\lambda,\mu}=
(i+R_1,\ldots,i+R_j,\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_a).
\]
Since
\[
R\subseteq\beta'\subseteq a^b\subseteq(q-i)^j,\quad
\lambda_1\le b\le i,\quad a+i\le q,\quad j+a\le r,
\]
this is an original wide decomposable partition in \(q^r\), of weight
\(ij+|\lambda|+|\mu|=ij+N\). Projecting \((*)\) to
\(\overline\Lambda\otimes\overline\Lambda\) and applying injectivity of \(T\) yields
\[
\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\rho)=
\sum_{\substack{\lambda,\mu\\\mu\ne\varnothing}}
(-1)^{|\mu|+1}c_{\lambda,\mu}^{\beta}\,
\operatorname{Lin}_{\varphi}(\nu_{\lambda,\mu}).
\tag{**}
\]
Hence every tall row is an integral combination of original wide rows, with every original coordinate retained. Any solution with wide right sides zero has every tall right side zero, contradicting a nonzero tall right side. This proves the required large-\(N\) inconsistency directly, without enlargement.

For the stated counterexample, \(\beta=(2)\), and \((**)\) is
\[
\operatorname{Lin}(2,2,2)
=\operatorname{Lin}(3,2,1)-\operatorname{Lin}(3,3),
\]
i.e.
\[
(1,0,1)=(1,1,1)-(0,1,0)
\]
in full column order
\[
(A_{\varnothing,(2)},A_{\varnothing,(1,1)},A_{(1),(1)}).
\]

## Gaps
No gap remains for this scoped alternative inconsistency certificate. It does not validate the false enlargement/projection argument or assert any parent-theorem conclusion.

## Next
The requested certificate is established by the full-coordinate integral identity \((**)\).
